options.label: The mortgage over the land is signed but not yet registered with the authorities

client.name: Hawally Hypermarket Group
client.profile: Successful three-branch grocery retailer, client for 6 years. Wants to open three more branches. A junior analyst pre-reviewed the file and recommended declining for 'severe liquidity weakness'.

request: "Three new branches, KD 2,100,000 of fit-out and equipment. Term loan, please. Also — your analyst sent us a worrying note about our 'liquidity problem'. We don't have a liquidity problem. Do we?"

ratios.label: Current ratio
ratios.hint: Frightening out of context. In context: see the working capital line below.

ratios.label: Working capital cycle
ratios.hint: NEGATIVE cycle: customers pay cash today; suppliers wait 92 days. Suppliers fund the whole operation and 54 days of float besides. For grocery retail this is strength, not distress.

ratios.label: DSCR on requested TL (6 yrs)
ratios.hint: Comfortable on existing cash flow, before the new branches contribute anything.

decisions.prompt: Was the analyst right about the 0.6x current ratio — and why?

options.label: Wrong — negative working capital is the grocery model’s strength
options.feedback: Suppliers fund the operation; that’s excellence, not distress.

options.label: Partly right — velocity risk deserves a covenant
options.feedback: The model’s one real weak point, correctly priced.

options.label: Right — sub-1.0x is a hard stop anywhere
options.feedback: Ratio fundamentalism would decline every supermarket on earth.

options.label: The financials conflict — unreliable
options.feedback: Every number tells one coherent retail story.

options.label: Hire a consultant to be sure
options.feedback: The pack already contains the answer.

options.label: Customers pay at the till; suppliers wait 92 days
options.feedback: The cash arrives before the bills do — structurally.

options.label: Benchmarks belong to sectors, not textbooks
options.feedback: A contractor at 0.6x drowns; a grocer thrives.

options.label: Ratios don’t matter for retail
options.feedback: They matter — read against the right model.

options.label: The analyst used stale numbers
options.feedback: The numbers were current; the reading wasn’t.

options.label: DSCR is the only ratio that counts
options.feedback: One ratio never tells a whole story.

decisions.prompt: Build the expansion financing.

options.label: Term loan for the fit-out — no working capital line needed
options.feedback: New branches generate cash from day one of trading.

options.label: Lease-finance hybrid on equipment
options.feedback: Workable alternative structure.

options.label: TL + STRL 1,000K "to be safe"
options.feedback: A working capital line for a negative-working-capital business.

options.label: Overdraft KD 2,100,000
options.feedback: Six-year assets on a daily swing line.

options.label: Decline per the analyst’s memo
options.feedback: A 1.7x DSCR client lost to a misread ratio.

options.label: KD 2,100,000 — all three branches
options.feedback: Proven operator, comfortable coverage before new revenue.

options.label: KD 1,400,000 — two branches first
options.feedback: Staging a plan that arguably doesn’t need it.

options.label: KD 3,000,000 with buffer
options.feedback: KD 900K of buffer with no purpose.

options.label: KD 700,000 — one branch
options.feedback: Underbacks a 14.5M-revenue operator’s plan.

options.label: KD 2,100,000 at 50% cash margin
options.feedback: Blocked cash from a supplier-financed retailer — the misread, priced.

options.label: 6 years
options.feedback: 1.7x coverage, matched to fit-out life.

options.label: 7 years
options.feedback: Slightly looser, still sensible.

options.label: 3 years
options.feedback: Heavy instalments for no reason.

options.label: 10 years
options.feedback: Outlives the fit-out being financed.

options.label: 12 months
options.feedback: Retail margins cannot repay 2.1M in a year.

decisions.prompt: Security and the covenant that watches the model’s real weak point.

options.label: Lien on fit-out & equipment + corporate guarantee
options.feedback: Proportionate, and the assets exist.

options.label: Lien + personal guarantees of partners
options.feedback: Equally defensible.

options.label: Mortgage over the branch premises
options.feedback: The branches are leased — nothing to mortgage.

options.label: 100% cash margin
options.feedback: Still pricing the misdiagnosis.

options.label: Clean
options.feedback: KD 2.1M unsecured when easy security exists.

options.label: Minimum monthly sales per new branch
options.feedback: Velocity is the model’s heartbeat — watch it.

options.label: Maximum payable days at 95
options.feedback: Guards the supplier financing the model rests on.

options.label: Current ratio above 1.2x
options.feedback: Would put every healthy month in breach.

options.label: Annual audited financials only
options.feedback: A year is an eternity in grocery velocity.

options.label: None

facilitySummary: Term Loan KD 2.1M / 6 years (3 new branches)
learn: Ratios mean nothing without the business model: negative working capital is distress in contracting and excellence in cash retail. Benchmark within the sector — and covenant the model's actual weak point, not the textbook's.

client.name: Sulaibiya Steel Fabrication
client.profile: Aggressive operator who doubled the company in 18 months. Charismatic, persuasive, always in a hurry. Account conduct has developed cracks the growth story doesn't mention.

request: "Revenue has DOUBLED in eighteen months and the order book is overflowing. I need all limits up 50% — today, ideally. Banks that move slowly lose clients like me. Are you a bank that moves slowly?"

figures.label: Gross margin
figures.hint: He's buying the growth — winning orders on price.

figures.label: Account conduct
figures.value: 2 returned cheques in 4 months ('technical errors'); 3 excesses over OD limit, regularised late

ratios.label: Leverage (Debt / Equity)
ratios.hint: Past the line and climbing — the growth is debt all the way down.

ratios.label: Working capital absorption
ratios.value: Every dinar of profit + new debt is consumed by WIP and receivables
ratios.hint: Classic overtrading mechanics: the order book eats cash faster than it returns it.

ratios.label: Interest cover
ratios.hint: Margin erosion and debt growth compounding into the same number.

decisions.prompt: Strip away the charisma: diagnosis and the strongest signal.

options.label: Late-stage overtrading: debt-fed growth at collapsing margins
options.feedback: All four gauges agree.

options.label: Growth timing issues — the order book will cure it
options.feedback: At 8% margins, each new order consumes more cash than it returns.

options.label: Healthy expansion, normal growing pains
options.feedback: The next stage of these pains is insolvency.

options.label: Exit now — the cheques are enough
options.feedback: A managed tightening can still save the money.

options.label: Competitor sabotage rumours
options.feedback: The balance sheet did this by itself.

options.label: Leverage, margins, payables and conduct all pointing one way
options.feedback: Four independent gauges, one story.

options.label: Two returned cheques in four months
options.feedback: The public symptom of the private exhaustion.

options.label: Interest cover collapsing to 1.4x
options.feedback: Margin erosion and debt growth compounding.

options.label: Revenue +105%
options.feedback: Growth is the setting, not the signal.

options.label: His urgency in the meeting
options.feedback: Charisma reads as confidence either way.

decisions.prompt: He is across the desk, waiting for his 50%. Set decision and conditions.

options.label: No increases; secured basis + capital plan + monthly accounts
options.feedback: The intervention that can still work.

options.label: Approve the +50%
options.feedback: Leveraging an overtrader past the point of return.

options.label: +20% compromise
options.feedback: Smaller fuel, same fire.

options.label: Freeze utilisation, demand early repayment
options.feedback: Converts a salvageable client into a certain loss.

options.label: Reassign the file to another RM
options.feedback: The risk stays on the bank’s book either way.

options.label: Capital injection plan within 60 days
options.feedback: The company needs equity, not debt — say so with a date.

options.label: Monthly management accounts
options.feedback: Shows within a quarter whether he heard you.

options.label: Reprice +0.5% and carry on
options.feedback: Half a percent extra on money you’re about to lose.

options.label: Owner’s verbal commitment
options.feedback: Verbal capital absorbs no losses.

options.label: Serve an exit letter today
options.feedback: Escalation has an order; this skips it.

decisions.prompt: The two returned cheques — meaning, and your next step.

options.label: Near-conclusive cash exhaustion — the buffer is gone
options.feedback: Companies pay cheques before almost anything.

options.label: Genuine technical errors, twice
options.feedback: Twice, during a visible cash squeeze, is a story.

options.label: Only matters if our cheque bounces
options.feedback: Same cash pool repays everyone.

options.label: A pricing opportunity
options.feedback: Risk action first; pricing follows structure.

options.label: Banking system glitches are common
options.feedback: Not twice in four months at one company.

options.label: Verify via credit bureau + supplier references
options.feedback: Conduct intelligence from outside his narrative.

options.label: Daily account-conduct monitoring
options.feedback: Watch the cash in real time.

options.label: Take his word and move on
options.feedback: His word is the thing under test.

options.label: Ask him to stop writing cheques
options.feedback: Treats the symptom’s visibility, not the cause.

options.label: Share concerns informally with other banks
options.feedback: Improper, and potentially a run you started.

facilitySummary: Limits held; capital plan required (Sulaibiya Steel)

plantedError.prompt: While re-papering the lines onto a secured basis, documentation runs its checks. What surfaces?
exhibit: Re-papering pack — all lines moving to secured basis
Board resolution on file — 3 years old, names GM 'Adel M.' as sole authorised signatory
Commercial registry extract — Adel M. resigned from the company last year
New facility documents — drafted, awaiting signature

options.label: The board resolution on file names a general manager who left the company a year ago as sole authorised signatory
options.feedback: Correct — every document signed since his departure is potentially voidable. A current board resolution and updated signatory cards are needed before any re-papering. Authorisations age; check them at every major event.

options.label: The file uses the company's old logo on some documents
options.feedback: Branding has no legal weight — signatures and authorisations do.

options.label: Nothing — proceed with re-papering
options.feedback: The signatory authorisation is a year out of date and names someone who left. That invalidates the chain — fix it first.

learn: Overtrading endgame: doubling revenue at collapsing margins, financed by suppliers and debt, until the cheques start bouncing. The cure is equity and discipline — never more debt. And returned cheques are never 'technical errors' twice.
